items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the real property tax law and the education law, in relation to payment of state aid for school tax relief within ninety days after application to the commissioner of taxation and finance
items.lawCode: Amd §1306-a, RPT L; amd §3609-e, Ed L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5109

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the real property tax law and the
education law, in relation to payment of state aid for school tax
relief within ninety days after application to the commissioner of
taxation and finance

PURPOSE:

To ensure homeowners who are approved for state aid, receive it within
ninety days of receipt of their application.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section One: Amends the real property tax law to add that upon
approving an application for state aid, it shall be paid within ninety
days of receipt of the application by the commissioner.

Section Two: Amends the education law to add that payment of state aid
shall be made within ninety days of receipt by the commissioner of
taxation and finance beginning with the 2015-16 school year.

Section Three: Sets forth the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

New York State's School Tax Relief (STAR) Program provides significant
school property's tax relief to a number of homeowners with a
household income less than $500,000 by reducing the taxable value of a
home before the school tax rate is applied.

There are currently varying deadlines -set by local municipalities -
to submit your STAR application. Once an application is submitted,
homeowners can confirm they will be receiving the STAR exemption by
checking the tentative assessment roll when it's made available to the
public. The assessment roll indicates next to your property the the
type and amount of your exemption. The "tentative" assessment rolls
"usually" come out on May 1st, however, there is no mandated deadline
for when the rolls must be release. As a result, homeowners are often
left not knowing how much theirmuch needed exemption will be for or
when they will be receiving them.

Furthermore, homeowners who submit their application before the
deadline and qualify for STAR should not have to wait an undetermined
amount of time before receiving their exemptions. If there is a
deadline for the homeowner to submit their application, then there
should also be a deadline in which the NYS Department of Taxation and
Finance, Office of Real Property Services (ORPS) must act in
accordance with.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To Be Determined.


EFFECTIVE DATE:

Ninety days after it shall have become law.

summary: Requires payment of state aid for school tax relief within ninety days after application to the commissioner of taxation and finance.
